scenes.heading: Factors and multiples
scenes.sub: How many ways can you share 12 lollies fairly?
scenes.say: How many ways can you share twelve lollies fairly, with none left over? The answer comes from factors. In this video you'll learn what factors and multiples are, and some quick tests to check them.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: 12 chairs fit in rows of 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 12 with none left over
scenes.science: So 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12 are the factors of 12
scenes.breaks: You only own so many chairs, but multiples never stop — every number has infinitely many.
scenes.say: Imagine setting out twelve chairs in equal rows. Rows of one, two, three, four, six or twelve all work, with no chairs left over. Those row sizes are the factors of twelve. Rows of five don't work, so five is not a factor.

scenes.heading: Factors and multiples
points: Factor: divides in exactly (3 is a factor of 18)
scenes.say: A factor divides into a number exactly. Three is a factor of eighteen, because eighteen divided by three is six. Factors come in pairs: one times eighteen, two times nine, three times six. A multiple is the number times one, two, three and so on. The multiples of seven are seven, fourteen, twenty-one, and they never stop.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: List all the factors of 18.
scenes.say: Let's list all the factors of eighteen. Start with one times eighteen. Two times nine works, and so does three times six. Four and five don't divide exactly, and six is already in a pair, so stop. The factors are one, two, three, six, nine and eighteen.

scenes.heading: Divisibility tests
points: 3: digits add to a multiple of 3
9: digits add to a multiple of 9
scenes.say: Divisibility tests are shortcuts. A number is divisible by two if its last digit is even, and by five if it ends in zero or five. For three and nine, add up the digits. For example, two thousand one hundred and forty-five has a digit sum of twelve, so it divides by three, but not by nine.

scenes.heading: Don't mix them up
scenes.say: Don't mix them up. Factors fit into the number. There are only a few, and they're never bigger than the number. Multiples come from multiplying. There are infinitely many, and they're never smaller than the number. A made-up trick: factors fit, multiples multiply.

points: Factors divide in exactly, in pairs
Every number has 1 and itself as factors
Use the digit sum to test for 3 and 9
scenes.say: Quick recap. Factors divide in exactly and come in pairs. Multiples are the number times one, two, three and so on. Every number has one and itself as factors. Use the digit sum to test for three and nine. Now try the practice questions!
